title: Historical resume can generate incomplete SQL while reporting success
reasoning: The script opens the SQL output with createWriteStream before applying checkpoint filtering, so rerunning with the same --sql-file truncates prior generated SQL. It then skips checkpointed subject-term items and only writes pending work. Because checkpoint entries are saved when SQL is generated, not when it has been applied to D1, an interrupted run followed by the documented rerun path can produce a SQL file missing already-checkpointed rows. The same flow commits and exits normally even when some subjects failed, leaving automation able to apply a partial historical corpus.
reproduction: Run with --sql-file historical.sql, allow a batch to complete so historical-sync-checkpoint.json is saved, interrupt before applying the SQL, then rerun the same command. The output file is recreated while checkpointed items are skipped, so the regenerated SQL lacks the first batch.
recommendation: Do not checkpoint generated rows as complete unless the resume path preserves their SQL. Either append safely to the same SQL file, regenerate all checkpointed SQL into the resumed output, or checkpoint only after an apply step. Also exit nonzero when any subject fails unless an explicit partial-output flag is provided.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: scripts/__tests__/historical-sync.test.ts covers parser and SQL helper behavior, but it does not execute main, checkpoint creation, resume, output truncation, or failed-subject exit behavior.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an integration-style test with mocked fetch/parser and a temp cwd: run once until after checkpoint/save, rerun with the same --sql-file, and assert the final SQL still contains the first batch or the command refuses to proceed.
minimumFixScope: scripts/historical-sync.ts checkpoint/output lifecycle and failed-subject exit handling.
